why.data/matches_levels.json: 3.11 (owner: the puzzles of Easy are too hard, the difficulty has to grow step by step). The three pools are one ladder now: every puzzle has a tier from 1 to 10 (how hidden its idea is, docs/games/matches.md § 10), and within a pool the tier never goes down. Easy — 7 puzzles of tiers 1-2: the answer is in plain sight (a square to close, a square to take off), 1-5 matches; six are new, the seventh is the original 'add 5 matches to make 9 squares'. Medium — 16 puzzles of tiers 2-4, one idea each (a larger square counts too, squares may touch at a corner, a square is given up to make two); thirteen are new. Hard — 34 puzzles of tiers 4-10: the puzzles of the original (the six that stood on Easy since 3.3 are of tiers 4-6 here) and six new ones of tiers 4-5 on the 2x3 and 3x3 grids, so that the ten steps do not start with a wall. A level with a 'rule' takes any board that does what its task says (games/matches-model.js ruleSolved); the check of the original compared the board with its reference boards only, and on seven puzzles it called right answers wrong (tools/analysis/matches_review.mjs: 'remove 5 matches to leave 6 squares' has 76 answers, the references covered 20). Under a wrong check the game now says what is wrong: the number of squares, a match left over, too many matches moved. The steps (3 / 5 / 10) and the thresholds stay. Illustration (tools/analysis/train_balance_matches.mjs; the chance to solve a puzzle by its tier is an assumption set on the real play logs, docs/analytics/players-2026-11.md): the average player passes Easy in 3 games, Medium in 7 and Hard in about 44; a strong one in 3, 5 and 11; before, the average player met puzzles of tiers 5-6 on Easy. 3.12 (owner: the first puzzles of Medium are as easy as Easy; the difficulty has to be seen from the player's side): the tier is what the player does — moving is harder than removing, an irregular figure is harder than a row or a block, and one or two matches on a small board are tried in the head, so a hidden idea hardly matters there. Easy 19 puzzles (tiers 1–2), Medium 8 (3–4), Hard 34 (4–10); four new 'move 2' puzzles open Hard. The pool of unsolved puzzles keeps ids instead of numbers.
why.MG_matches_hard.level_up_param: 3.9 (owner: a review of Matches for balance; the rule he set for Roadblocks in 3.7 — a game without a time penalty gives a step only for a clean result). up 1 → 12000: the puzzle solved with at most one wrong check (15000 − 3000 for a wrong check). Before, any solved puzzle gave a step, even after four wrong checks, so the answer could be found by trying. One wrong check is forgiven on every level, because a check compares the board with the reference answers: an arrangement that fits the task but is not among them is possible. A puzzle solved with more wrong checks still leaves the pool and gives its points, but not a step. required 12 -> 10 with a hard pool of 16 puzzles: compound conditions (squares of different sizes, contiguous or nested squares, 14 squares, hexagons, equal figures) and 3-18 matches. Any 10 of the 16, so the four giants (10-18 matches, 10^8.5-10^15 candidate boards per solution) are not a wall: before all 12 hard puzzles were needed, including them. Proxy: average player 43 % of the dealt puzzles solved, 34 sessions for the level (74 before); strong 77 %, 10 sessions (36 before); novice 25 %.
why.matches_help.2_value: The original item 2 is the @TASK macro; the shell strips macros and the Rules box of Matches stayed empty (BUG-MAT-08). Item 4 (the rules text, translated in every locale) is shown instead; the game itself adds the task of the current puzzle to its rules.
why.MG_matches_easy.level_up_param: 3.9 (owner: a review of Matches for balance; the rule he set for Roadblocks in 3.7 — a game without a time penalty gives a step only for a clean result). up 1 → 3000: the puzzle solved with at most two wrong checks (5000 − 1000 for a wrong check); Medium and Hard forgive one. Before, any solved puzzle gave a step, even after four wrong checks, so the answer could be found by trying. Easy forgives one check more, as Easy forgives a lost ball in Roadblocks: with one check the proxy of tools/analysis/train_balance_matches.mjs gave the average player a step in 74 % of the sessions and the novice in 38 %, with two — 86 % and 49 % (the novice solves a dealt Easy puzzle in 69 % of the sessions at all; the wrong checks of the proxy are an assumption, the real logs so far show fewer). A check is forgiven on every level because it compares the board with the reference answers: an arrangement that fits the task but is not among them is possible. A puzzle solved with more wrong checks still leaves the pool and gives its points, but not a step. Owner: easy needs 3 steps in every game, and easy puzzles must be really easy. required 8 -> 3 with a re-sorted easy pool of 6 puzzles (data_changes): the six puzzles that change 1-2 matches on figures of 12-19 matches. A step is any solved puzzle (up = 1), so the level-up is any 3 of the 6 — a puzzle that does not come can be left. Before: 8 puzzles of 2-5 matches, all 8 had to be solved (the three 1-2-match puzzles of the game sat in the hard pool). Illustration with the solve-chance proxy of tools/analysis/train_balance_matches.mjs (assumption): the average player solves a dealt easy puzzle in 96 % of the sessions (75 % before), 3 sessions for the level (15 before). Unlock (4th number): level-ups needed to open the game. v3.3 (owner: the last games opened too slowly): 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 instead of 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 16, 18 — the average model player opens all 12 games in 23–30 trainings instead of 30–42 (tools/analysis/unlock_pace.py).
